#Aletheia #USPol

The campaign presented Platner as a populist veteran capable of winning working-class voters.
Stated Judgement: (+1.0, 0.0) — Good Preference

Unvetted personal history, including sexual assault allegations and controversial tattoos, led to a swift campaign collapse.
Resulting Judgement: (-1.0, 1.0) — Lesser Evil

Verdict: FAIL — The Path of Deception.
Promoting an unvetted candidate created a severe political liability and damaged party credibility.

Integrity: Severe Deception (R_net: 12.5, Uncertainty z: 4)
Maine Democratic Senate candidate Graham Platner withdrew from the race following sexual assault allegations, exposing a major vetting failure by his progressive backers.

The Bright Side:
The swift withdrawal of support by key progressive leaders shows that accountability was eventually enforced once the allegations surfaced.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
Confusing narrative appeal (WHY) with character fitness (WHO).

It is a structural bait-and-switch: promoting a populist hero who carried severe unvetted liabilities.

Social Physics Analysis:
By prioritizing narrative appeal over transparent vetting, organizers created a fragile coalition. The post-hoc defense of the candidate before his collapse reveals a self-serving loop.

The Trajectory: The Path of Deception.
When you map the gap between stated intentions and ground-level results, it plots a direct trajectory toward Lesser Evil. Vetting failures undermine political trust.

The Unavoidable Truth: Narrative-driven campaigns fail without rigorous vetting.

The Unavoidable Lie: The candidate's past was entirely unknown to local organizers.

Alethekanon:
The failure to perform basic due diligence on a high-profile candidate represents a severe systemic breakdown in political risk management.

Awwthekanon:
It is painful when a movement's hope is shattered by harmful behavior. We must prioritize safety and integrity to build true trust.
